0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog enforces that limit and is the only authority on whether it
0018| # elapsed: it records its decision in the private check directory, and the
0019| # installer reads the outcome only once that decision exists. A shell still
0020| # running when the limit elapses therefore fails the installation, whatever the
0021| # ordering of its exit and the decision. Nothing the check started outlives it:
0022| # the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it, are stopped on every
0023| # exit path. The installer then checks that ``forgel-code`` resolves to the
0024| # launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces the installation; running with
0025| # ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Environment variables:
0028| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0029| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0030| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0031| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.1.0)
0032| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0033| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)

0037| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)

0914| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:
0915|     """A handled shell name that records the check's directory, then runs ``real_shell``.
0916| 
0917|     ``ls -ld`` output of every ``forgel-code-check.*`` entry goes into ``probe``,
0918|     so the test can inspect the permissions of a directory that no longer exists
0919|     by the time the installer returns. The entries sit in the temporary tree of
0920|     the test, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0921|     """
0922|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0923|     stub = directory / "bash"
0924|     stub.write_text(
0925|         "#!/bin/sh\nprobe=%s\n" % _shell_quote(probe)
0926|         + 'ls -ld "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.* > "$probe/entries" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0927|         % CHECK_PREFIX
0928|         + 'exec %s "$@"\n' % _shell_quote(real_shell),
0929|         encoding="utf-8",
0930|     )
0931|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0932|     return stub

0935| def _late_login_shell(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0936|     """A handled shell that answers past the bound but claims the launcher resolved.
0937| 
0938|     Its login session sleeps past a one-second bound and then prints exactly the
0939|     report a successful check prints. It ignores the graceful stop, so its own
0940|     exit, and not a signal, is what ends it.
0941|     """
0942|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0943|     stub = directory / "bash"
0944|     stub.write_text(
0945|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0946|         "trap '' TERM\n"
0947|         "sleep 2\n"
0948|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
0949|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
0950|         "exit 0\n",
0951|         encoding="utf-8",
0952|     )
0953|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0954|     return stub

0957| def _late_login_shell_withholding_decision(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0958|     """A late shell that hides the watchdog's decision while it runs.
0959| 
0960|     It removes the write permission of the private check directory, so the
0961|     watchdog cannot record whether the bound elapsed, and restores it when it
0962|     exits past the bound, still printing the report of a successful check. The
0963|     directory is found the way the permission probe finds it: under the TMPDIR
0964|     the installer was given, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0965|     """
0966|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0967|     stub = directory / "bash"
0968|     stub.write_text(
0969|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0970|         "trap '' TERM\n"
0971|         "check_dir=\n"
0972|         'for candidate in "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.*; do\n' % CHECK_PREFIX
0973|         + '    [ -d "$candidate" ] || continue\n'
0974|         + "    check_dir=$candidate\n"
0975|         + '    chmod 500 "$candidate" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0976|         + "done\n"
0977|         + "sleep 2\n"
0978|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
0979|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
0980|         + 'if [ -n "$check_dir" ]; then\n'
0981|         + '    chmod 700 "$check_dir" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0982|         + "fi\n"
0983|         + "exit 0\n",
0984|         encoding="utf-8",
0985|     )
0986|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0987|     return stub

0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog enforces that limit and is the only authority on whether it
0018| # elapsed: it records its decision in the private check directory, and the
0019| # installer reads the outcome only once that decision exists. A shell still
0020| # running when the limit elapses therefore fails the installation, whatever the
0021| # ordering of its exit and the decision. Nothing the check started outlives it:
0022| # the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it, are stopped on every
0023| # exit path. The installer then checks that ``forgel-code`` resolves to the
0024| # launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces the installation; running with
0025| # ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Environment variables:
0028| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0029| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0030| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0031| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.1.0)
0032| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0033| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
0034| #   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
0035| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
0036| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
0037| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0038| #
0039| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.
0040| 
0041| set -eu
0042| 
0043| # The exact markers an uninstall looks for. They are compared byte for byte.
0044| MARKER_START='# >>> forgel-code >>>'
0045| MARKER_END='# <<< forgel-code <<<'
0046| 
0047| # A profile whose last line has no final newline cannot be restored byte for
0048| # byte from the block alone: the newline that separates that line from the
0049| # block is indistinguishable from one the file always had. The installer
0050| # records the case in one comment line directly above the block and removes
0051| # that line, with the separator newline, together with the block.

0680| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0681| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background and a watchdog
0682| # bounds it. The watchdog is also the only authority on whether the bound
0683| # elapsed: it records ``timed-out`` in the private directory before it starts
0684| # the graceful stop, and ``finished`` when it sees the command gone before the
0685| # bound. The caller waits, for at most DECISION_WAIT seconds, until that
0686| # decision exists and only then reads the outcome, so the ordering between the
0687| # command's exit and the marker write cannot turn a timed-out check into a
0688| # success. After the graceful stop the watchdog forcefully stops the rest of the
0689| # checked command's process group once the grace period has passed. Nothing the
0690| # function starts survives it. CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.

0692| # The checked command leads a process group of its own (see ``start_check``), so
0693| # the group is what the cleanup signals, on the success path as much as on the
0694| # timeout path. Its three standard descriptors are redirected, so the group has
0695| # no terminal to hold it and cannot stop on a terminal access.
0696| bounded_run() {
0697|     limit=$1
0698|     shift
0699|     CHECK_STATUS=0
0700|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0701|     CHECK_CLEANED=
0702|     CHECK_CHILD=
0703|     CHECK_GROUP=
0704|     if ! create_check_dir; then
0705|         return 1
0706|     fi
0707|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0708|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0709|     finished=$CHECK_DIR/finished
0710|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0711|     umask 077
0712|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0713|         umask "$saved_umask"
0714|         cleanup_check
0715|         return 1
0716|     fi
0717|     start_check "$out" "$@"
0718|     umask "$saved_umask"

0720|     (
0721|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0722|         sleeper=
0723|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0724|         elapsed=0
0725|         while [ "$elapsed" -lt "$limit" ]; do
0726|             sleep 1 &
0727|             sleeper=$!
0728|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0729|             sleeper=
0730|             elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
0731|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0732|                 # The command finished inside the bound; record that decision
0733|                 # so the caller never has to infer it from the exit alone.
0734|                 : > "$finished" 2>/dev/null || true
0735|                 exit 0
0736|             fi
0737|         done
0738|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0739|         stop_check TERM
0740|         sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
0741|         stop_check KILL

0746|         if [ -e "$timed_out" ]; then

0748|         fi
0749|         # The watchdog records its decision before it stops anything, so on
0750|         # the timeout path it may still own the graceful then the forceful
0751|         # stop; let it finish so nothing outlives the check.
0752|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0753|     else
0754|         # A watchdog that never answers is not allowed to hold the installer,
0755|         # and a decision that never arrives is never a successful check.
0756|         kill -KILL "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0757|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0758|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0759|     fi
0760|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0761|     # The check is released here, before any state the release reads is
0762|     # cleared: a successful check leaves nothing behind, exactly like a failed
0763|     # or a timed-out one.
0764|     cleanup_check

0914| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:
0915|     """A handled shell name that records the check's directory, then runs ``real_shell``.
0916| 
0917|     ``ls -ld`` output of every ``forgel-code-check.*`` entry goes into ``probe``,
0918|     so the test can inspect the permissions of a directory that no longer exists
0919|     by the time the installer returns. The entries sit in the temporary tree of
0920|     the test, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0921|     """
0922|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0923|     stub = directory / "bash"
0924|     stub.write_text(
0925|         "#!/bin/sh\nprobe=%s\n" % _shell_quote(probe)
0926|         + 'ls -ld "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.* > "$probe/entries" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0927|         % CHECK_PREFIX
0928|         + 'exec %s "$@"\n' % _shell_quote(real_shell),
0929|         encoding="utf-8",
0930|     )
0931|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0932|     return stub

0935| def _late_login_shell(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0936|     """A handled shell that answers past the bound but claims the launcher resolved.
0937| 
0938|     Its login session sleeps past a one-second bound and then prints exactly the
0939|     report a successful check prints. It ignores the graceful stop, so its own
0940|     exit, and not a signal, is what ends it.
0941|     """
0942|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0943|     stub = directory / "bash"
0944|     stub.write_text(
0945|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0946|         "trap '' TERM\n"
0947|         "sleep 2\n"
0948|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
0949|         "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
0950|         "exit 0\n",
0951|         encoding="utf-8",
0952|     )
0953|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0954|     return stub
0955| 
0956| 
0957| def _late_login_shell_withholding_decision(directory: Path, launcher: Path) -> Path:
0958|     """A late shell that hides the watchdog's decision while it runs.
0959| 
0960|     It removes the write permission of the private check directory, so the
0961|     watchdog cannot record whether the bound elapsed, and restores it when it
0962|     exits past the bound, still printing the report of a successful check. The
0963|     directory is found the way the permission probe finds it: under the TMPDIR
0964|     the installer was given, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
0965|     """
0966|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0967|     stub = directory / "bash"
0968|     stub.write_text(
0969|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
0970|         "trap '' TERM\n"
0971|         "check_dir=\n"
0972|         'for candidate in "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.*; do\n' % CHECK_PREFIX
0973|         + '    [ -d "$candidate" ] || continue\n'
0974|         + "    check_dir=$candidate\n"
0975|         + '    chmod 500 "$candidate" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0976|         + "done\n"
0977|         + "sleep 2\n"
0978|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-path=%s\\n' '/usr/bin:/bin'\n"
0979|         + "printf 'forgel-fresh-resolved=%s\\n' " + _shell_quote(launcher) + "\n"
0980|         + 'if [ -n "$check_dir" ]; then\n'
0981|         + '    chmod 700 "$check_dir" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0982|         + "fi\n"
0983|         + "exit 0\n",
0984|         encoding="utf-8",
0985|     )
0986|     stub.chmod(0o755)
0987|     return stub

0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:

0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,

0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
